title: Deleting a digest leaves stored article content orphaned

evidence.quote: content: str = Field(... description="Full article content (HTML or Markdown)")
Links processed articles to their parent digest. ... digest_id: UUID = Field(foreign_key="digests.id", index=True)

reasoning: The route deletes only the Digest row. DigestArticle rows store the full article content and are linked by digest_id, but there is no explicit delete of those rows and no ORM/database cascade shown. In this SQLite setup, foreign keys are not enabled by the engine, so the delete can succeed while leaving private article content orphaned and unreachable through normal digest APIs.
reproduction: Create a completed digest with DigestArticle rows, call DELETE /api/digests/{filename}, then query digest_articles for the deleted digest_id. The article rows and their content remain.
recommendation: Delete associated DigestArticle rows in the same transaction before deleting the Digest, or define and verify cascade behavior. Include any other digest-scoped records that should be removed with a digest.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: There are no delete route tests, and the existing tests that create DigestArticle rows only exercise PDF download generation.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a delete test that creates a digest with two DigestArticle rows, deletes the digest, and asserts both the Digest and its DigestArticle rows are gone.
minimumFixScope: Update delete_digest to remove digest-scoped child records transactionally; add a regression test for child cleanup.
